title: PerformanceTest
description: Canonical, engine-neutral description of a performance test. The web UI, the REST API and YAML/GitOps all produce exactly this document. Engine-specific plans are generated from it after validation; consumers never author JMX or Playwright harness configuration directly.

apiVersion.description: Schema version. Pinned so a future schema change is an explicit migration rather than a silent reinterpretation.

name.description: Lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens. Names appear in artifact object keys and Kubernetes labels, which are length-limited and character-restricted.

duration.description: A duration such as 30s, 5m, 2h or 90d. ISO-8601 (PT5M) is also accepted.

threshold.description: An objective threshold with an explicit unit. A unit-less value is rejected rather than assumed, because a mis-scaled threshold silently changes a test's pass/fail outcome.

secretRef.description: A reference to a credential held in the approved secret manager. Never the credential itself: this document is stored, rendered, returned by the validate endpoint and often committed to Git, so an inline value is a disclosure.

team.description: Owning team. Every authorization decision starts here.

labels.description: Free-form metadata for search and reporting. Never used for policy decisions.

runnerCell.description: The execution cell that runs the workload. Determines which targets are reachable.

targetClass.description: Drives approval policy. Declared here but verified server-side against the application's registered environments — a specification cannot promote its own target to a safer class.

type.description: k6 is not an accepted source type in this release.

uri.description: Stored artifact reference for document sources, including reviewed Playwright scripts.

digest.description: SHA-256 digest of uploaded or pasted Playwright script content. Required with artifact-backed Playwright sources so the reviewed source is immutable.

repository.description: An https or ssh clone URL, which must be on the deployment's allowlist (platform.orchestration.playwright.allowed-repositories). A test cannot choose where its code is fetched from, for the same reason it cannot choose its own target host. The URL must not carry credentials: a specification holds references, never secret values.

ref.description: An immutable commit SHA. A branch or tag is rejected: it can move after review, so the code that ran would not be recoverable from the stored version.

path.description: Test path relative to the repository root. Must not escape the checked-out workspace.

injectAs.description: The request header name the runner injects when a workload references this authentication entry, for example Authorization or X-Api-Key.

uri.description: The stored dataset version this test reads, as dataset://<name>/<version> — the uri POST /api/v2/datasets returns. The version is required: without it, two runs of the same immutable test version would read different rows while carrying the same specification digest.

columns.description: Column names this test expects the dataset to have. A scenario binds to one with ${name} in its path, query, headers or body. Declared here because validation is side-effect-free and runs before any file is attached; the file's own header is compared against this before the run starts, so a re-exported dataset cannot silently bind different values to the same names.

partitionByShard.description: When true, each shard receives a non-overlapping slice. When false and the run is sharded, every generator replays the same rows, which distorts results and can duplicate writes to the target.

engine.description: Requested engine. Validated against declared engine capabilities. k6 is not approved for this release.

sourceRef.description: Name of a source declared under spec.sources.

authRef.description: Name of an authentication entry to inject for this workload.

startWhen.description: Starts this workload when another reaches a named stage. Used to measure a browser cohort during protocol steady state.

browserUsers.description: Concurrent browser sessions. Budgeted separately from protocol virtual users: a browser session costs orders of magnitude more, so these are never counted against the same ceiling.

browserProfile.description: Browser measurement profile. Web-vital objectives are only comparable when device, network and CPU throttling are stable.

device.description: mobile, desktop or a named Playwright device.

loadModel.description: Load, stress, spike and endurance tests are all expressed as a staged shape; the platform models the shape rather than naming fixed test types. Two shapes: stages holds a number of concurrent users and lets throughput be whatever they produce, and arrival-rate sends a stated number of requests per second whatever the system does with them. See docs/operations/load-models.md.

maxConcurrency.description: The most requests allowed in flight at once. Required for arrival-rate and refused for stages, where the user count is the concurrency. In an open model a stalled target accumulates in-flight requests without bound until the generator itself fails and the run reports that as the target's failure. Admission control budgets against this number, never against the rate.

name.description: Optional stage name used by browser workloads that start during a protocol load boundary.

targetUsers.description: Concurrent users, for a stages model. Stage order is significant: stages run in sequence, and a final stage targeting zero expresses ramp-down.

targetRate.description: Requests per second, for an arrival-rate model. A final stage targeting zero expresses ramp-down.

scenario.description: A weighted journey. Weights are what produce a realistic traffic mix instead of an even spread across every endpoint. A scenario says what to call either directly, with method and path, or by referring to an imported operation with operationId.

weight.description: Relative share of iterations. Weights across a workload should sum to 100.

operationId.description: Reference to an operation in an imported source. Resolved from Increment 2 onward; until then such a scenario addresses /{operationId}, which is deliberately obvious rather than plausible.

method.description: HTTP method. Defaults to GET when omitted.

path.description: Request path, relative to the base URL the platform resolves for this application. Never a full URL: where a run's traffic goes is decided by the team's registered targets, not by the specification.

headers.description: Request headers. Never credentials: Authorization, Cookie, X-Api-Key and similar are refused outright, and any value shaped like a token is rejected. Authentication belongs in spec.authentication as a reference the runner resolves at execution time.

query.description: Query parameters appended to the path. Never credentials: a query string is written to every access log between the runner and the target.

body.description: The request body, for methods that carry one. A bare string is shorthand for {content: "..."}.

contentType.description: Media type sent. Defaults to application/json, and is written as a Content-Type header so the target does not reject the request.

steps.description: The ordered requests this journey makes. A scenario states either one request, through method and path, or a list of steps -- never both. Steps are what let a journey sign in and carry the session forward.

objective.description: The pass/fail contract. A test with no objectives can neither pass nor fail.

scope.description: Workload this applies to. Omit to apply to the whole test.

percentile.description: An explicitly measured percentile; 100 is the maximum. Other percentiles are rejected.

correlationHeader.description: Injected into workload traffic so application telemetry can be correlated to this run.

maxDuration.description: Ceiling for this test. Enforced server-side alongside the platform limit; the lower of the two applies.

name.description: Identifies this step in results and findings.

method.description: HTTP method. Defaults to GET when omitted.

path.description: Request path, relative to the base URL the platform resolves for this application. Never a full URL: where a run's traffic goes is decided by the team's registered targets, not by the specification.

headers.description: Request headers. Never credentials: Authorization, Cookie, X-Api-Key and similar are refused outright, and any value shaped like a token is rejected. Authentication belongs in spec.authentication as a reference the runner resolves at execution time.

query.description: Query parameters appended to the path. Never credentials: a query string is written to every access log between the runner and the target.

body.description: The request body, for methods that carry one. A bare string is shorthand for {content: "..."}.

contentType.description: Media type sent. Defaults to application/json, and is written as a Content-Type header so the target does not reject the request.

extract.description: Values taken out of the response for later steps to use. A failed extraction is never silent: the engine substitutes a sentinel and an assertion fails the sample, because an unfilled reference is sent as literal text and the run would otherwise report fast, healthy-looking latency for a target that did no work.

expect.description: What must be true of the response. Without a correctness check, a load test of a broken deployment reports excellent numbers for a wall of 500s.

thinkTime.description: How long a user pauses after this step, e.g. '2s'.

extraction.description: A value pulled out of a response, referred to later as ${name}.

name.description: The ${name} later steps use. Must not collide with a dataset column, or the reference would have two sources.

from.description: Where in the response to look.

expression.description: A JSON path, a regular expression with exactly one capturing group, a header name, or a cookie name -- whichever 'from' calls for. Not needed for 'status'.

required.description: Whether the journey can continue without it. True by default, and rarely worth changing: an optional extraction still produces its sentinel, but nothing fails when it does not match.

assertion.description: What must be true of a response.

value.description: The status code, the text, or the pattern.
